nodes.name: C10 - Point-set triangulation
nodes.summary: Lecture notes extending triangulation from polygons to arbitrary planar point sets, covering legal triangulations and angularly optimal triangulations.

nodes.name: C11 - Voronoi diagrams
nodes.summary: Lecture notes on Voronoi diagrams, Delaunay triangulations, Fortune-style sweep-line construction, event handling, and planar subdivisions represented with DCEL.

nodes.name: C12 - Intersections
nodes.summary: Lecture notes on segment and polygon intersections, algebraic complexity, event/status structures, sweep-line methods, output-sensitive results, and thematic layer overlay.

nodes.name: C13-14 - Linear programming elements
nodes.summary: Lecture notes on half-plane intersections, mold extraction motivation, geometric duality, qualitative half-plane reasoning, and linear programming in geometric settings.

nodes.name: C8 - Convex hulls
nodes.summary: Lecture notes introducing computational geometry, numerical criteria, orientation tests, point ratios, convex hulls, Graham scan, Jarvis march, and divide-and-conquer hull construction.

nodes.name: C9 - Polygon triangulation
nodes.summary: Lecture notes on the art gallery problem, polygon visibility, ear clipping, monotone polygon triangulation, dual graphs, and 3-coloring arguments.

nodes.name: Computational geometry exam model
nodes.summary: Exam model for the computational geometry module with multiple-choice and open questions spanning C8 through C13-14 topics.

nodes.name: Seminar 5 exercises
nodes.summary: Exercise sheet for weeks 9 and 10 covering collinearity ratios, orientation determinants, Graham scan convex hull traces, and divide-and-conquer convex hull analysis.

nodes.name: Seminar 5 solutions
nodes.summary: Worked solutions for Seminar 5 exercises, including collinearity computations, orientation tests, Graham scan lower hull evolution, and convex hull divide-and-conquer reasoning.

nodes.name: Seminar 6 exercises
nodes.summary: Exercise sheet for weeks 11 and 12 covering Jarvis march, art gallery camera placement, triangulations, convex and concave vertices, and convex hull counting cases.

nodes.name: Seminar 6 solutions
nodes.summary: Worked solutions for Seminar 6 exercises, explaining Jarvis march pivot tests, art gallery triangulation/coloring, polygon examples, and convex hull counting cases.

nodes.name: Computational geometry curriculum
nodes.summary: The overall sequence of course materials for advanced algorithms topics in computational geometry.

nodes.name: Convex hull algorithms
nodes.summary: Orientation-based methods for computing convex hull boundaries, including Graham scan, Jarvis march, and divide-and-conquer strategies.

nodes.name: Triangulation methods
nodes.summary: Polygon and point-set triangulation techniques used for art gallery arguments, monotone polygons, and legal triangulations.

nodes.name: Voronoi and Delaunay structures
nodes.summary: Nearest-site subdivisions, Delaunay duality, sweep-line construction, and DCEL representation of planar subdivisions.

nodes.name: Sweep-line intersections
nodes.summary: Event-driven algorithms for detecting segment and polygon intersections with status structures and output-sensitive behavior.

nodes.name: Duality and linear programming
nodes.summary: Half-plane intersections, point-line duality, and optimization problems framed as geometric linear programming.
